newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland, April 11.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland, April 11.

text.p: The following are the highlights of stories from the Irish press on Friday.

- Senior security sources suspect the shooting of a Northern Ireland police officer in Londonderry may mark the beginning of a renewed campaign by the Irish Republican Army of attacks on police and British army targets along the border.
- Ireland has joined its EU partners in withdrawing its Ambassador from Iran after a German court ruling that Tehran ordered the 1992 killings of four Kurdish dissidents.

- A draft of the Irish government coalition's common election manifesto has been completed by party strategists and will be discussed by the three party leaders at a pre-cabinet meeting next Thursday.
- Irish police investigating the murder of journalist Veronica Guerin were still detaining seven people in Dublin last night.
- The rate of Ireland's inflation remains moderate, with the latest figures showing prices rose by only 0.1 percent last month.

- Finex, the Dublin futures exchange, is looking at the possibility of introducing a futures product based on the Dublin ISEQ equity index, as well as restarting the now defunct Irish Futures and Options Exchange (IFOX) bond and interest rate futures exchange.
- The opening of a number of big British chain stores in Dublin is helping keep inflation at a surprisingly low level.
- The Irish Republican Army gave a brutal response on Thursday to rumours of a ceasefire when it shot a policewoman in Derry.
- A self-confessed prime suspect for the murder of Irish journalist Veronica Guerin is to appear in a Dublin court today on drug distribution charges.
